subject: CHEMISTRY
description: Disciplinary ontology, Johnstone triad representations, and validation invariants for Grade 9-11 Chemistry (CBSE, JEE Main, JEE Advanced).

FOUNDATION.name: CBSE_BOARD
FOUNDATION.target: Atomic structure (Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr), valency, chemical bonding (ionic/covalent), balancing equations, periodic table groups, states of matter.

STANDARD.name: JEE_MAINS
STANDARD.target: Stoichiometry and mole concept, redox balancing (ion-electron and oxidation number methods), chemical equilibrium and Le Chatelier principle, thermochemistry cycles, VSEPR shapes.

RESEARCH.name: JEE_ADVANCED
RESEARCH.target: Molecular orbital theory diagrams, complex redox disproportionation mechanisms, non-ideal gas equations, multi-step thermodynamics cycles, kinetics rate laws and transition state theory.

epistemological_rules: Enforce Johnstone's Triad: every chemical concept must bridge macroscopic observables, submicroscopic particulate models, and symbolic representations.
Mass and charge conservation: all nuclear atom counts and net algebraic charges must balance across reaction arrows.
Oxidation numbers must adhere strictly to IUPAC rules; fractional states must be grounded in structural resonance or non-equivalent atom environments.
Electron configurations must strictly satisfy Aufbau principle, Hund's rule, and Pauli exclusion principle (maximum 2*n^2 capacity per shell).
